name: M-13 service manual

pages.title: Barrel heating zones
pages.text: M-13's barrel has four heating zones and a nozzle heater. Zone 3 is heated by heater band HB-60 and read by thermocouple TCJ-2 on PLC input M13_Z3_TEMP. The PLC switches the band through solid-state relay SSR-3, driven by PLC output M13_Z3_HEAT. Setpoints for caps and closures: zone 1 200 °C, zone 2 215 °C, zone 3 225 °C, zone 4 230 °C, nozzle 235 °C.

pages.title: Alarm A-203: zone 3 under temperature
pages.text: When M13_Z3_TEMP stays more than 25 °C under setpoint for five minutes, the PLC raises alarm A-203. Check in this order. 1. On the HMI, M13_Z3_HEAT is on while the zone is cold: the indicator LED on SSR-3 must light. If it stays dark, the output or its wiring has failed: call the electrician on call. 2. With the machine locked out and the band below 50 °C, heater band HB-60 reads 20 to 25 ohms across its terminals. Open, or 0 ohms, means a failed band: replace it (page 40). A loose terminal on a band replaced recently is the most common cause: re-torque it to 2 N·m. 3. Thermocouple TCJ-2 reads within 5 °C of a handheld probe at the same point; if it does not, replace it.

pages.title: Short shots
pages.text: A short shot is a part that does not fill. On M-13 the usual causes are a cold barrel zone (alarms A-203 and A-204), a nozzle tip NT-3 partly blocked, a worn check ring, or a shot size set too low. Rule out a cold zone first: a zone 30 °C or more under setpoint thickens the melt enough to short-fill a closure.

pages.title: Replacing a heater band
pages.text: 1. Lock out and tag M-13 and verify zero energy. 2. Let the band cool below 50 °C. 3. Photograph the terminal wiring, then disconnect it. 4. Loosen the clamp screw and slide the band off the barrel. 5. Fit the new HB-60 band in the same position, clamp screw to 4 N·m. 6. Reconnect the wiring as photographed, terminals to 2 N·m. 7. Remove the lockout, heat up, and confirm M13_Z3_TEMP reaches setpoint within 20 minutes without alarm A-203.
